references.text: Describes the rings through which the poles are to be inserted to carry the ark
The same construction principle of poles through rings is used for the altar of burnt offering
The altar of incense also has rings and poles to be carried in the same way
Fulfillment of the command to insert the poles into the rings on the ark
Moses sets up the ark with the poles as described in the instructions
The sons of Kohath were to carry the holy objects, including the ark, using the poles
The Kohathites carried the holy things on their shoulders with the poles
The poles were so long that they could be seen from the Holy Place, and they remained there
Parallel text to 1 Kings 8:7-8 regarding the poles in the ark in the temple
Parallel instruction for carrying holy objects (the ark and the altar) emphasizing the mobility of God's presence
Thematic parallel showing that the principle of carrying poles and rings was consistent across various holy furnishings
Thematic connection demonstrating unity in construction principles for carrying different holy objects
Construction details highlighting consistency in how carrying poles are attached to various holy objects
Thematic parallel showing common material use (acacia wood and gold) for holy carrying poles across different furnishings
